Layer 4 (variance): null-model dispersion, decomposition and per-gene SE

Source: R/estimateVariance.R
estimateVariance.Rd

For every comparison, fits the chosen DE method and returns the per-gene standard error of the two-group log2 fold-change contrast (used by estimateSensitivity()). The SE uses the dispersion estimated with the condition in the design, as the user's test sees it, evaluated at the condition-blind (null-model) fitted means. Power is always computed at the target effect, never the observed one. A null-model dispersion would absorb real effects as noise and understate power exactly where DE is strong. The variance decomposition stays condition-blind. For the count methods (edgeR, deseq2) it also splits the pseudobulk negative-binomial dispersion phi_total into a cell-heterogeneity term (theta/n, with the cell-level theta from pbSetup()) and a between-donor term phi_donor (moment estimate max(0, phi_total - theta*mean(1/n))), and reports the depth/cell/donor variance shares with a regime label. The voom method uses limma's precision-weight variance model, so it has no NB decomposition (those columns are NA).

Usage

estimateVariance(x, method = c("edgeR", "deseq2", "voom", "dreamlet"))

Arguments

x

A S4Vectors::SimpleList from pbSetup().

method

One of "edgeR", "deseq2", "voom" (or the reserved "dreamlet"). Default "edgeR".

Value

A list with summary (a data.frame, one row per comparison, with the method, the NB decomposition and regime) and pergene (a named list of per-comparison fits carrying se_log2 and df for sensitivity, and the method's own p-values for the condition, pvalue, behind the pi1 = "discoveries" mapping in estimateSensitivity()).

Details

The method should match the differential-expression method the user intends to run. edgeR and deseq2 require sum aggregation (integer counts); voom works on either sum (voom) or mean (limma-trend) pseudobulks. dreamlet is reserved for mixed designs and is not yet implemented.
